item.name: Ambulance Event
item.trigger: Dr. Harlow announces an anomaly attack on the town, starting from about shift 4 or 5, and six patients rush in at once.
item.resolution: Treat all six incoming patients and grab whatever rooms are open; some arrive on fire or critically injured, so prioritize the most urgent cases.
item.toolsNeeded: Fire extinguisher plus standard treatment supplies
item.notes: After you clear the first ambulance, the event returns roughly every five shifts with more critical patients and a cash bonus if you finish the wave.
item.cardSummary: A surge event where six patients flood the hospital together, some on fire or critical. It is the only emergency that stacks several crises at once, so it tests how fast you can triage.

item.name: Room Fire
item.trigger: A room randomly catches fire during a shift, before or after a patient checks in.
item.resolution: Put out the flames with the fire extinguisher, or smother them with your hands if you have no extinguisher yet.
item.toolsNeeded: Fire extinguisher (kept in the glass case near the check-in booth; usable after completing 2 shifts)
item.consequence: Standing in the fire drains about 1-3 sanity per second, and patients faint if they walk into a burning room.
item.notes: There is no countdown, but clear it fast because it blocks you from treating the patient in that room.
item.cardSummary: A room bursts into flames and stays dangerous until you extinguish it. It has no death timer, but the sanity drain and fainting risk make it an urgent fix.

item.name: Patient on Fire
item.trigger: A patient runs into the hospital fully on fire, panicking and screaming.
item.resolution: Spray them with the fire extinguisher for an instant heal, or put the fire out by hand and then treat the burns with ointment, all within the timer.
item.toolsNeeded: Fire extinguisher (preferred) or hands plus burn ointment
item.consequence: The patient dies if the 60-second timer runs out.
item.notes: The extinguisher is the fastest fix; the hands-and-ointment route takes longer and risks missing the timer.
item.cardSummary: A patient arrives engulfed in flames and you have one minute to save them. The extinguisher clears it instantly, making it the go-to tool for this emergency.

item.name: Patient Fainted
item.trigger: A patient faints at check-in, after walking into a burning room, after being shot, or after being tased.
item.resolution: Pick the fainted patient up and carry them to their designated bed before the timer ends.
item.consequence: The patient dies if not bedded in time.
item.notes: Standard faint timer is 60 seconds; fainting from fire is about 40 seconds. Throwing a fainted patient in the trash removes them without counting as a death, but it also forfeits their reward. Shooting an already fainted patient kills them.
item.cardSummary: A patient collapses and must be carried to their bed before the timer ends (usually one minute, shorter if they fainted from fire). No tools are needed, just quick lifting and good room awareness.

item.name: Critical Patient
item.trigger: A patient arrives in critical condition, often as part of the ambulance wave.
item.resolution: Run the full treatment process for them, from check-in through every required care step, before the timer expires.
item.toolsNeeded: Varies with the treatment the patient needs
item.consequence: The patient dies if the full treatment is not finished in time.
item.notes: Individual critical timers often sit around one to two minutes and stop once recovery starts, not only when the patient hits the bed. Start these first during ambulance waves.
item.cardSummary: A patient shows up needing complete care against the clock. The challenge is finishing every treatment step, not a single quick fix.

item.name: Death Ritual
item.trigger: In an occupied room the door creaks open slowly, the lights dim, the patient floats, and ritual candles fill the room.
item.resolution: Snuff out every candle one by one, tase the patient to break the ritual instantly, or clear candles with eyedrops, IV drops, or coffee.
item.toolsNeeded: Taser (free at the start of shift 3, recharges in its box) or eyedrops / IV drops / coffee
item.consequence: The patient dies if the ritual completes before you stop it.
item.notes: Candle count is not fixed in every guide; clear the full set before the 40-second timer ends. Hollow-eyed and twitching admits are strongly linked to rituals. Tasing is fastest; eyedrops, IV drops, or coffee can clear candles with less sanity loss than snuffing by hand.
item.cardSummary: A floating patient is surrounded by lit ritual candles and you have 40 seconds to break the ritual. The taser ends it quickly, but clearing the candles also works.

item.name: Bed Monster
item.trigger: A monster grabs a patient and slowly drags them underneath the bed.
item.resolution: Equip maple syrup (or organ or transplant as an alternate feed), enter the red zone carefully, and feed the monster so it releases the patient. You can also feed it before a grab to clear the under-bed threat.
item.toolsNeeded: Maple syrup (primary); organ or transplant as alternate feed
item.consequence: The monster eats the patient if you do not feed it within 30 seconds.
item.notes: The monster can grab players too, so approach the red zone with the syrup ready.
item.cardSummary: A monster pulls a patient under the bed and you have only 30 seconds to react. Feeding it maple syrup is the way to make it let go.

item.name: Tendril (Room 8)
item.trigger: Purple tendrils emerge from a recovering surgery patient in Room 8.
item.resolution: Complete the surgery mini-game again by following the on-screen treatment steps for the Room 8 procedure.
item.consequence: The patient dies if the mini-game is not finished in time.
item.notes: Officially named Tendril on the wiki and enemy list. Do not tase or shoot the purple tendrils; attacking them kills the patient instantly.
item.cardSummary: A purple Tendril erupts during Room 8 recovery and must be cleared with the surgery mini-game. Weapons kill the patient, so this is the emergency you never tase.
